1) Feeling aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 31.08.2017 passed by learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxi.), Palanpur, Banaskantha District (which shall hereinafter be referred to as "the Tribunal" for short), in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.26 of Parmar Roshniben Dilipkumar vs Hareshbhai Mafatlal Allsanga on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29700702/
1 2017, the appellants - original claimants have preferred the present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (which shall hereinafter be referred to as "the Act" for short).

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2782/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/02/2026 undefined 2) Heard learned Advocate Mr. K. K. Thakkar, for the appellants - original Claimants and learned Advocate Mr. R. P. Raval, for the respondent no.2 - Insurance Company.
Perused the original record and proceedings.

3) It is the case of the appellants that on 14.01.2017, the deceased Dilipbhai Galababhai Parmar (who shall hereinafter be referred to as "deceased") was coming from Danta to Palanpur in offending vehicle being Motorcycle bearing Reg. No.GJ-08-AG-5503, when on the highway road of sim of Jalotra Village, the driver of opponent no.1 was driving the Jeep bearing Reg.
No.GJ-08-A-3799, in rash and negligent manner and dashed with the motorcycle and due to which the deceased got serious injuries on chest and died.
Therefore, the appellants had filed MAC Petition seeking compensation, wherein, the learned Tribunal after appreciating the evidence produced on record has partly allowed the claim petition.

4) Learned Advocate for the appellants - claimants has submitted that the learned Tribunal has committed error in assessing the income of the deceased only Rs.5,000/- which is required to be considered as per minimum wages as Rs.8,000/- per month.
He has further submitted that the Tribunal also erred in awarding meagre amount towards other heads and not awarded loss of consortium to each of the member of the family.

He has further submitted that the learned Tribunal has also committed error in mechanically holding NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2782/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/02/2026 undefined the deceased 50% negligent without any documentary or oral evidence in this regard.

He has further submitted that merely driving a vehicle or being behind the wheels itself not a reason to presume contributory negligent and it must be proved that the person driving was negligent in causing the accident.
With these submissions he has requested to allow the present appeal.

5) Learned Advocate for the respondent - Insurance Company has opposed the present appeal on the ground that the learned Tribunal has rightly assessed the income of the deceased in absence of evidence of income and properly appreciated the evidence produced on record and awarded the compensation.
Hence, he has requested to dismiss the present appeal.

6) Having heard the learned Advocates for the respective parties and going through the record it appears that the learned Tribunal has considered the evidence on record and relied on the judgment in the cases of Bimla Devi Vs. H.R.T.C, reported in AIR 2009 SC 2819, and Parmeshwari Devi Vs.
Amir Chand, reported in 2011 (11) SCC 635, and appreciated the evidence based on preponderance of probabilities.

sentences.text: So far the issue of negligent is concerned, a perusal of complaint at NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2782/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/02/2026 undefined Exhibit 24, reveals that the complaint was lodged by Sureshbhai Jethabhai Parmar who is not the eye witness of the accident.
The panchnama at Exhibit 25, reveals that the place of accident is lying on East to West direction and the width of the road is 20 feet.
The deceased was riding the motorcycle from east to west while the Jeep was approaching from west to east.
The front wheel plate, tyre, meter box of the Jeep were totally broken and damaged, whereas, the motorcycle suffered approximate damage.
The Jeep was going from Palanpur to Danta with its right side facing north and the motorcycle was proceeding from west to south with its right side facing south.
The left side of the Jeep got damaged.
The learned Tribunal, after considering the aforesaid facts, attributed contributory negligence equally at 50% of the deceased and 50% of the Jeep driver.

However, having regard to the relative sizes of the vehicles, their positions at the time of accident, the width of the road and the variance between the proof and pleadings, this Court is of the considered view that the negligence of the deceased is required to be reduced from 50% to 25% and negligence of the Jeep driver is considered to the extent of 75% in causing the accident.

Therefore, up to that extent the learned Tribunal has committed error and interference is required to modify the impugned judgment to the extent that the deceased is held 25% negligent, whereas, the driver of Jeep is 75% negligent in the occurrence of the accident.

8) Now coming to the quantum part, as per the law laid down by the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2782/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/02/2026 undefined Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Govind Yadav Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd., reported in 2012(1) TAC 1 (SC), that if no proof of income is produced on the record then Tribunal has to consider prevalent minimum wages in absence of evidence of monthly income of the deceased.

entities.text: Govind Yadav Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd., reported in 2012(1) TAC 1 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case the accident occurred on 14.01.2017 and during that time the deceased was doing Electricl Wiring Work and was earning Rs.10,000/-, whereas, the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased as Rs.5,000/- per month which is required to be enhanced as per the rate of minimum wages of the prevalent time and hence, the income of the deceased is reassessed as Rs.7,700/- per month.

Further, as the deceased was aged 32 years at the time of accident but the learned Tribunal has committed error in considering future prospective income as 50%, however, considering the age of the deceased and the fact that deceased was not having any permanent job therefore 40% addition towards future prospectus is considered.

Moreover, as the deceased was having 5 dependents 1/4 deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and multiplier of 16 were considered by the learned Tribunal as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt) & Ors. Vs.
Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. [2009 (6) SCC 121] which are just and proper.

sentences.text:
9) Therefore, recalculating the income of the deceased as Rs.7,700/-
and future prospect of 40% = Rs.3,080/- which comes to NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2782/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/02/2026 undefined Rs.10,780/- and 1/4 amount is required to be deducted towards personal living expenses of the deceased which comes to Rs.2,695/- and the net amount comes to Rs.8,085/-.
In view of above the amount under the head of future loss of income is required to be reassessed as Rs.8,085/- x 12 x 16 = Rs.15,52,320/-.
Therefore, the appellants are entitled to get additional amount of Rs.4,72,320/- towards future loss of income.

666, the learned Tribunal has committed error in awarding only Rs.60,000/- towards loss of consortium, however, in view of above judgments the appellants - original claimants being legal heirs of the deceased they are entitled for Rs.48,400/- each towards the head of loss of consortium.

Therefore, the appellants are entitled for additional amount of Rs.1,82,000/- under the head of loss of consortium.
